findings.title: Duplicate method definition silently overrides the first `downsize`
findings.body: Two `self.downsize` methods are defined (lines 145 and 149). In Ruby the second definition completely replaces the first, so the 4-argument version `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` is dead code. Any existing callers in the codebase that invoke `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height)` will now have `width` interpreted as the `dimensions` string and `height` interpreted as `opts`, producing incorrect behavior or errors.

findings.title: Using the same file path as both input and output for ImageMagick `convert`
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` passes the same path as source and destination. ImageMagick's `convert` command opens the output file for writing (truncating it) before it finishes reading the input, which can produce an empty or corrupted file. A safe approach is to write to a temporary file and then replace the original.

findings.title: Upload proceeds even if downsize loop fails to reduce size below the limit
findings.body: After the while-loop (lines 66-69), execution unconditionally falls through to `Upload.create_for` on line 72. If after 5 iterations the image is still larger than `max_image_size_kb`, the oversized image is stored anyway, defeating the purpose of the feature. There should be a check after the loop to reject or further handle images that could not be reduced to the allowed size.

findings.title: Client-side max size is hardcoded, ignoring the admin-configured site setting
findings.body: The client-side validation now always allows uploads up to 10 MB regardless of the `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` site settings. If an admin configures a smaller limit, users will not see a client-side error until the server responds, and the error message shown (line 184) will incorrectly state the limit is 10 MB. The original code correctly read from `Discourse.SiteSettings`.

findings.title: Tempfile read position may be stale after in-place modification by shell command
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` writes to `tempfile.path` via a shell command, bypassing the Ruby Tempfile IO object. If the Tempfile's internal file descriptor has been read from or seeked (e.g., by a prior `.size` call on some Ruby versions or by `Upload.create_for` expecting position 0), subsequent reads from the Tempfile may return empty or partial data. Calling `tempfile.rewind` after the downsize loop would make this safe.

findings.title: Download limit for API URL uploads is hardcoded to 10 MB regardless of site setting
findings.body: The original code used `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` as the download cap, preventing excessively large downloads. Now any URL up to 10 MB will be downloaded even if the admin has set a much lower limit, increasing bandwidth and memory usage on the server for sites with restrictive settings.
